- Prior coaching: 3 documented coaching notes in Aug/Sep/Oct 2026; we had a formal mid-quarter improvement chat on 2026-10-14.

I've kept the tone supportive in the template and listed concrete, measurable objectives (deliverable deadlines, review turnaround times, and a monthly quality metric). If Legal recommends softer phrasing in the consequence section, I'm happy to adjust.

Thanks for the draft, Olga — good work pulling together specifics. A few quick items from People Ops: 

1) Timeline: I generally prefer 45 days for IC execution roles; it gives a clearer midpoint calibration and reduces open-ended risk. However, if you can show the examples need more runway, 60 is OK. Recommend we agree 45 days by default and allow an extension with documented progress.

2) Objectives: Please add an explicit weekly check-in cadence (15–30m) and a clear set of owner-verified deliverables for each two-week sprint. That reduces disputes about "completion."

3) Evidence: We need written examples of the two production incidents with timelines (who was notified, remediation steps) — the attached PDF is a good start but please add any Slack threads or pager logs as appendices.

4) Manager responsibilities: Add a short section on coaching notes and how we'll document each checkpoint (email summary after each session).

5) Process note: I recommend we avoid formal "termination if unmet" phrasing in the first notice — instead use: "Failure to make measurable progress may result in further corrective action up to and including termination." Legal will confirm exact wording.

I'm copying Lauren for workforce impact (headcount/role change) if we anticipate reallocation during the support window. If you want, I can run the template past our external consultant for best-practice wording.

I'll be available for a quick review tomorrow at 2pm PT.

—Monica

Olga / Monica — reviewed. High-level legal guidance below. Attaching a redlined doc to the Google Draft (link in metadata).

- Language: Monica's suggested phrase is fine. Do not include absolute termination deadlines in the first notice. Use conditional language and describe the escalation steps (written CSN -> formal improvement plan -> final warning) rather than immediate termination.
- Evidence: Ensure all evidence is factual, dated, and includes source (PR number, Slack thread timestamp, incident ticket id). Avoid speculative wording about intent.
- Privacy & accommodation: Add a one-paragraph statement offering an opportunity to request reasonable accommodations if performance issues are related to a disability — standard safe practice.
- Signatures & approvals: For a non-exempt IC, have manager + HR sign the CSN; for any role where termination could materially affect a customer, include Legal signoff before sending.
- Severance/appeal: Do not promise severance in the notice; keep appeals to existing company grievance procedures. If you anticipate a short-term transfer or role change, route that through Lauren for repackaging.

Process checklist I need before signoff:
1) Finalized CSN language (doc or Google draft)
2) Compiled evidence appendix (PRs, tickets, Slack slices)
3) Confirmation of meeting time for notice delivery (manager + HR present)
4) People Ops headcount note if role will be backfilled during support window

I can sign off after those items are complete. If you want me to run a brief call with the external counsel (copied earlier in our thread historically), I'm happy to do that tomorrow morning.

—Markus Klein
General Counsel (Interim)
